scheme_name: Capital Subsidy Scheme for Setting Up Solar Plant in Milk Cooperatives in Gujarat State (Tribal Area)
description:
The Capital Subsidy Scheme for Setting Up Solar Plant in Milk Cooperatives in Gujarat State (Tribal Area) was launched on January 1, 2021. 

This scheme aims to promote renewable energy use in the dairy sector, particularly in tribal areas of Gujarat. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to milk cooperatives for the installation of solar power plants. 

The government aims to enhance energy security and reduce dependency on conventional energy sources. 

The scheme specifically targets milk cooperatives operating in tribal regions of Gujarat. 

The government has set a target to install solar power plants with a total capacity of 10 megawatts by the end of the financial year 2023. 

The benefits of this scheme include a capital subsidy of up to 30 percent of the total project cost. 

The maximum subsidy amount available under this scheme is ₹1 crore. 

This subsidy is intended to cover the cost of solar panels, inverters, and other necessary equipment. 

Additionally, the scheme aims to reduce the electricity bills of milk cooperatives significantly. 

By utilizing solar energy, cooperatives can save up to ₹5 per unit on their electricity costs. 

This translates to substantial savings over time, especially for large-scale operations. 

Eligibility for this scheme is limited to registered milk cooperatives in the tribal areas of Gujarat. 

The cooperatives must be operational for at least three years to qualify for the subsidy. 

The annual turnover of the cooperative should not exceed ₹10 crore. 

The cooperative must also demonstrate a commitment to sustainability and renewable energy practices. 

The application process for the Capital Subsidy Scheme involves several steps. 

First, eligible cooperatives must submit a detailed project proposal to the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF). 

The proposal should include technical specifications, project cost estimates, and expected energy savings. 

Required documents include the cooperative's registration certificate, annual financial statements, and a resolution from the cooperative's managing committee. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it will be reviewed by a technical committee formed by the GCMMF. 

If approved, the cooperative will receive a letter of sanction detailing the subsidy amount. 

The cooperative must then complete the installation of the solar plant within six months of receiving the sanction letter. 

After installation, the cooperative must submit a completion report along with photographs of the installed solar plant. 

The disbursement of the subsidy will occur within 30 days of the submission of the completion report. 

The scheme is implemented by the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation in collaboration with the Gujarat Energy Development Agency (GEDA). 

The contact details for GEDA are as follows: GEDA Office, Sector 10A, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, PIN - 382010. 

The phone number for GEDA is +91-79-232-560-00. 

The email address for inquiries is geda@gujarat.gov.in. 

The scheme is part of the larger initiative by the Government of India to promote solar energy under the National Solar Mission. 

The National Solar Mission aims to achieve a solar power generation capacity of 100 GW by 2022. 

This scheme aligns with the mission's goals by promoting solar energy in rural and tribal areas. 

The implementation of solar plants in milk cooperatives is expected to create job opportunities in the local community. 

It will also contribute to the overall economic development of tribal areas in Gujarat. 

The scheme is expected to benefit approximately 200 milk cooperatives in the state. 

Each cooperative is expected to generate around 100 kW of solar power on average. 

This will lead to a cumulative generation of 20 million units of electricity annually. 

The reduction in carbon footprint due to the use of solar energy is another significant benefit. 

The scheme is also expected to enhance the reliability of electricity supply for milk cooperatives. 

This is particularly important for operations that require a constant power supply for refrigeration and processing. 

The government has also emphasized the importance of awareness and training programs for cooperative members. 

These programs aim to educate members about the benefits of solar energy and proper maintenance of solar equipment. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to empower tribal communities through sustainable practices. 

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of renewable energy reach the most marginalized sections of society. 

The Capital Subsidy Scheme for Setting Up Solar Plant in Milk Cooperatives in Gujarat State (Tribal Area) is a crucial step towards achieving these goals. 

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to promoting green energy solutions. 

It also highlights the importance of cooperative movements in rural development. 

The success of this scheme could serve as a model for similar initiatives in other states. 

Overall, the scheme is a significant initiative aimed at transforming the dairy sector in Gujarat's tribal areas. 

It combines economic development with environmental sustainability. 

The expected outcomes include increased energy efficiency and reduced operational costs for milk cooperatives. 

The scheme is a clear indication of the government's focus on renewable energy and rural development. 

The implementation of this scheme will be closely monitored to ensure that the objectives are met. 

Regular assessments will be conducted to evaluate the impact of the solar plants on the cooperatives' operations. 

The government is hopeful that this initiative will lead to a sustainable future for the dairy sector in Gujarat. 

In conclusion, the Capital Subsidy Scheme for Setting Up Solar Plant in Milk Cooperatives in Gujarat State (Tribal Area) is a well-structured program. 

It provides essential financial support to enhance the use of renewable energy in the dairy industry. 

This scheme is expected to bring about significant changes in the lives of those involved in milk cooperatives in tribal areas. 

The focus on sustainability and economic empowerment makes this scheme a vital part of India's development agenda.
